1.title: Pilot

candidates.text: A documentary crew turns up at the Scranton paper company for the first time, filming the staff at their desks.
candidates.grounded_in: A documentary crew arrives at the Scranton, Pennsylvania, offices of Dunder Mifflin to observe the employees and learn about modern management.

candidates.text: A young temporary worker starts his first day at the branch and is shown around the office.
candidates.grounded_in: The office also gets new employee Ryan Howard (B. J. Novak) as a temporary worker

candidates.text: For the cameras, the regional manager insists everything at the branch is wonderful and morale could not be better.
candidates.grounded_in: Regional manager Michael Scott (Steve Carell) tries to paint a happy picture in the face of potential downsizing from corporate.

1.note: Very sparse summary; also, every named character debuts here, so probes describe roles rather than naming people.

candidates.text: Michael tapes index cards with different races written on them to everyone's foreheads and makes them act out stereotypes.
candidates.grounded_in: assigns each staff member an index card with a different race on it

candidates.text: An outside consultant arrives to run a tolerance session, and Michael keeps interrupting to deliver his own version.
candidates.grounded_in: A consultant named Al Brown (guest star Larry Wilmore) arrives to teach the staff about tolerance and diversity, but Michael insists on imparting his own knowledge

candidates.text: The whole office is herded into the conference room for a mandatory seminar about race and tolerance.
candidates.grounded_in: forces the staff to undergo a racial diversity seminar

candidates.text: Jim and Pam entertain themselves filling out the medical forms Dwight has handed around the office.
candidates.grounded_in: Jim and Pam amuse themselves with Dwight's medical forms

candidates.text: Dwight is put in charge of picking the office's new health care plan, and takes the job very seriously.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael puts Dwight in charge of choosing the company's new health care plan

candidates.text: Michael promises the whole office a big surprise, then spends the day scrambling to come up with one.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael promises the entire office a surprise, and then spends the rest of the day scrambling to come through with his promise

4.title: The Alliance

candidates.text: Michael spends the whole day agonizing over what joke to write in a coworker's birthday card.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael agonizes over writing the perfect greeting in her birthday card

candidates.text: The office holds a morale-boosting birthday party for an employee whose birthday is over a month away.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael arranges a morale-boosting birthday party for Supplier Relations representative Meredith Palmer (Kate Flannery), although her birthday is more than a month away

candidates.text: With downsizing rumors swirling, paranoia spreads through the office and Dwight starts talking in Survivor terms.
candidates.grounded_in: As downsizing rumors swirl, paranoia takes over the members of the office.

4.note: The episode's central thread is Dwight forming an alliance with Jim and Pam, which rule 1 excludes as a new alliance; remaining material is thin.

candidates.text: The office staff square off against the warehouse crew in a basketball game, losers owing a Saturday shift.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael and the office staff take on the workers in the warehouse in a basketball game, with the losers having to work on Saturday.

candidates.text: Michael assembles his lineup by looks and assumptions, passing over the more athletic office workers for weaker players.
candidates.grounded_in: Through racist and sexist ideals, Michael chooses many of the lesser skilled office workers over their more athletic peers.

candidates.text: Michael stops play mid-game to insist on a "flagrant personal intentional foul" against his side.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael claims a "flagrant personal intentional foul", stops the game

candidates.text: A visiting saleswoman sets up a table of purses in the office, and the men keep drifting over.
candidates.grounded_in: an attractive purse saleswoman named Katy (Amy Adams) comes to the office

candidates.text: Michael and Dwight openly compete for the attention of the woman selling handbags out of the conference area.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael and Dwight openly vie for her attention

candidates.text: An espresso machine turns up in the office kitchen, courtesy of Michael's spending.
candidates.grounded_in: Michael spends the money on an espresso machine

candidates.text: Corporate sets aside a thousand dollars as a prize for the branch's top salesman.
candidates.grounded_in: the corporate office allocates $1,000 as a prize for the top office salesman
